name: fzf-bd4efa27-misled30
instr:
# fzf misreads keys, miscounts rows and misorders matches — diagnosing it without a test suite

This is an interactive filter: you hand it a list of lines, it draws them on the screen, and as you type it narrows the list and hands back what you picked. A fresh build of it misbehaves in a startling number of unrelated places, so this is everything I could pin down from the outside, entirely by using it. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits.

Start it up and the trouble begins before anything is drawn. It asks the screen where the cursor sits, then whether bracketed paste is on, then where the cursor sits again; even when all three replies come back promptly and in order, the row and column it settles on are the ones you would see if nothing had been read at all. The clearing it does afterwards is off too: the number of erase sequences it writes to wipe out a reply the screen echoed back does not match how far that echo actually reached. Once it is drawing, printing two coloured words followed by two plain ones produces a byte stream with the ordinary printable letters missing, as though each of them were an unprintable control code. Colours are mistranslated as well — one given as six digits in base sixteen comes out with its red, green and blue taken from the wrong digits, so a request for pure red is not red — and when a colour state is turned back into an escape sequence, the reverse-video attribute is always tacked on, so even a plain foreground chang
